title: ReArch dependency/call graph
description: Canonical shape for a resolved graph snapshot (output of the link pass, then the cluster pass adds `cluster`). Node IDs are stable across commits so version-aware diffing can key on them directly.

id.description: Stable ID: '<language>:<relative_path>:<qualified_symbol_name>'. Must not depend on DB auto-increment IDs so diffing survives renames/moves being detected as such rather than as spurious add+remove. Overloaded methods in Java/C#/PHP get a '~2', '~3' suffix so every definition has its own node.

bases.description: Base classes, interfaces and traits for kind=class, as written in source (not yet resolved to node IDs).

params.description: Parameter declarations as written, for functions and methods.

cluster.description: Subsystem id assigned by the cluster pass; -1 means unassigned (modules and unresolved placeholders are never clustered).

namespace.description: Java package, C# namespace or PHP namespace, dotted. Set on classes (and PHP top-level functions).

returns.description: Declared return type of a Java/C#/PHP method with wrappers like Task<T> removed; used to type `var x = recv.method()`.

is_interface.description: True for Java/C#/PHP interfaces: calls through one resolve to its declaration, not to an implementation.

target.description: Node ID of the callee/imported symbol/base class, OR an 'unresolved:<raw expression>' placeholder ID when resolution fails.

resolution.description: resolved = single unambiguous static target. dynamic = fan-out over a known finite set (e.g. dict-based dispatch) but the exact runtime target can't be determined statically. inferred-http = cross-language edge guessed from matching route/URL string literals, never asserted as certain. unresolved = target symbol could not be found at all (e.g. calling a bare local variable with no traceable origin).

evidence.description: Short human-readable justification, e.g. the matched route string or the dict literal name that produced a dynamic fan-out.

external.description: Present on an unresolved edge whose root is a known library, so the migration plan can say which subsystem depends on which framework.

kind.description: library = known to be outside the project but which of several imported namespaces it came from is not known.
